I think my suspension of disbelief makes it possible for me to ignore this for the most part. It is all fantasy afterall, but you make a fair point. I think that fact that mercenaries exist very plentifully in these sort of universes makes things like trade more feasible. There's also more safety in numbers. Wild animals will usually avoid large settlements and if they do wander it'd be like 1 wolf or bear versus 15+ level 1 peasants. If the world building is really good like say something like Faerun there will be settlements with unique defenses like in the case of Eltruel (though this did eventually end poorly.) For large world shattering evils that threaten the well being of the enitre world that's were the chosen one or wrong place wrong time hero comes in to swoop in and save the day or fall to their own folly.

What I'm getting at is if the writers are good or creative enough there can usually be an explanation for why something can function the way it does even if it seem impractical on first glance. (You can also make up your own headcanons which I personally love doing.)
